first_nonempty_rows: There are four tabs in the XLSX, which correspond to the four "processed" files (as well as to physical 96-well plates). In the ScalePlex system, those four 96-well plates go through 3-4 levels of mixing (effectively, re-plating) to build up a combinatorial single-cell index (which is the column 'barcode' in each sheet). The combinatorial system is how we go from four 96-well plates to around ~770 raw FASTQs. Running those FASTQs through the ScalePlex computational library demultiplexes the ~770 FASTQs into the four 'processed' .MTX files and assigns the cell barcodes; at this juncture, since we are back to the original four 96-well plates, we can map the experimental conditions for those cells -- the treatment, age, and cell line.
